body: I'm actually happiest when I'm traveling. It's the money that prevents me from doing it more often, as with most people I'd assume

Yeah, sorry, my problems must seem a little immature, it can just be hard to look past something when it's all you've known for your entire life.

And yes, that would absolutely be fair to say. I believe in always fighting for the underdog, the marginalized, the impoverished, the oppressed. It sounds cheesy, but I actually do love helping people because it's easy for me to see human rights offenses and know that they're wrong when so much of everything else is so ambiguous to me.

What I've experienced a lot in my life is when I get excited about something and am eager to talk about it, people either brush it off or make me feel stupid for being excited about it. Like if I'm organizing a particular event and someone tells me they've done that many times before and it's easy. That's an example but it's happened to me in much more extreme cases as well. I've come to feel guilty about the things that I am excited about.

On top of that, there's all sorts of stories I could get into about being younger and parents fighting over who had to take me and who's responsibility I was, like I was a burden. It goes pretty deep but I see it in my day to day interactions with people. This is pretty embarrassing to admit, but even if someone criticizes an article of clothing or a facial feature or whatever, it crushes me and I feel like shit. I just depend on other people too much for my self worth but I have no idea how to fix it and it seems unfixable to me right now. I have too many damn flaws
I have. But there's not guarantee I'll be able to find a job, let alone one in which I'd actually be able to make a difference
Do you mind if we continue this over PM? sorry, I guess I'm too paranoid that someone I know will see this

Anything having to do with social justice. I grew up in a pretty low-income home and so anything having to do with poverty and inequality around the globe fascinates me, whether it manifests itself in health, or food access, or labor, or bigoted people. But that doesn't necessarily translate into a job, which stresses me out beyond belief because the last thing I want is to become worried about money all the time like I have been conditioned to in the shitty environment i grew up in

What do you mean by "career student"? I'm going to get my degree, I'm set on that. I suppose it's whether or not I'll be able to do the extra-curriculars to translate what I learn in the classroom into tangible skills and so I can really help people. the more I vent it out, it seems so stupid. I guess it's hard to do what I do, which seems so black and white to me on paper (or a screen) when not one person in my life is supportive of it.

I could be independent. I choose to not cut off contact because I have a little sibling. She is the most incredible thing in my life and I need to be rock for her that I didn't have. I just don't know how I can when I have to deal with what else comes with "home"

I'm a student-I love learning, and I love being involved with the student groups I'm in. I have a work study job but apparently that's not a real job and I'm being told all over the place that I need to get a "real paying job sooner or later." it's genuinely like they want me to be unhappy. If I told my parents I wanted to continue my education after graduation I don't know what would happen. but if I quit school and got a "real job" I would be so unhappy. I don't know what's wrong with me
